sections.preamble: You are a coding assistant running inside pi, a coding agent harness. Help users inspect files, run commands, and modify code.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- write: Create or overwrite files
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call

Additional tools may be available.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Use edit for targeted changes. Batch changes to one file in a single call.
- Each edits[].oldText must exactly and uniquely match the original file. Keep matches short and non-overlapping; merge nearby changes without including large unchanged regions.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

content.text: Generate an animated SVG of an anteater riding a unicycle while juggling bottles.

content.thinking:
**Generating Anteater Animation**

I'm currently considering the best output method for the animated SVG: should I write it to a file, like `anteater-unicycle.svg`, or output the SVG code directly?

**Crafting Animated Anteater**

I've decided to generate the animated SVG directly to a file named `anteater-unicycle.svg`. I'm now focusing on the visual details of the scene, aiming for a warm circus backdrop with a dynamic, moving ground to imply motion. The unicycle's design, including its wheel and spokes, is also being carefully considered.

**Designing Anteater Details**

I'm working on the anteater's pose, ensuring it looks balanced on the unicycle with a slight lean. Key features like the bushy tail with gentle sway, the distinct shoulder stripe, and the long snout are being animated. I'm also focusing on the leg movement to match the pedal rotation.

**Animating Anteater Actions**

I've figured out how to make the anteater's legs perfectly follow the unicycle's pedals using `<animate attributeName="d">` with keyframes, ensuring smooth rotation. The front paws are now in motion, set up to toss and catch juggling bottles in sync with the action.

**Juggling Bottle Dynamics**

I've implemented the juggling cascade with three distinct bottles. They are now following parabolic arcs and spinning end-over-end, timed precisely to create a continuous, visually engaging cycle. I'm also verifying the compatibility of these SMIL animations across standard SVG viewers.

**Verifying Animation Timing**

I'm currently focused on ensuring all SMIL animation timings are mathematically precise. This includes verifying wheel rotation, ground scrolling loops, and meticulously calculating pedal keyframe positions for a smooth, consistent cycle. All elements are designed for native browser compatibility.

**Refining Leg and Juggling Paths**

I've successfully mapped out the opposite pedal's rotation, ensuring a precise $\pi$ shift for natural leg movement. Using `<animate attributeName="d">` with these pedal coordinates is allowing for realistic leg bending and pedaling. I'm now defining the juggling bottle paths, focusing on a smooth 3-bottle cascade with a figure-8 motion between hands.

**Adjusting Juggling Arcs**

I'm refining the juggling bottle paths, correcting a misconception about the figure-8. I've now mapped out a true two-arc cascade with appropriate parabolic throws and catches for both hands, ensuring the bottles reach a consistent peak height and scoop cleanly.
